newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX volatilities off despite weak dollar.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX volatilities off despite weak dollar.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options were off Thursday's lofty levels at U.S. midsession despite the dollar's weakness as weekend time-decay weighed on the market, dealers said.
"Vols have really come off a lot since yesterday, basically people digesting the Japanese forex policy that's coming out now," said a trader at a U.S. bank in the West Coast.
Even though the spot dollar remained weak, it managed to hold above Thursday's lows just above 111 yen and a psychological support at 1.50 marks, traders noted.
One-month dollar/yen implied volatility stood at 8.3/8.5 percent in late U.S. morning, down from Thursday's peak of about 9.9 and closing near 9.0.

The dollar fell sharply on Thursday on remarks by an influential Japanese Finance Ministry official known for his role in taming the raging yen last year that the dollar's comeback from postwar lows was about over.

"I don't think you can declare the dollar's uptrend is over yet," said a European bank trader in New York. "But clearly, people are looking more at the downside now and that's where volatility is going to be."

Japanese exporters, who had been a non-factor in the dollar's bull run in the past few months, were now back in the market to hedge their dollar exposures and pushed risk reversals deep in favor of yen calls.

Risk reversals reflect pricing differential for puts and calls. One-month 25-delta risk reversal in dollar/yen stood unchanged from Thursday at 0.7/1.0 percent skewed toward yen calls after staying pegged near par for weeks.
Dollar/mark implied volatilities were also softer, with one-month volatility a tenth of a point below late Thursday levels at 7.8/8.0 percent.
One-month risk-reversal stood at 0.45/0.75 percent in favor of mark calls.

While most traders said dollar/mark in itself had not seen aggressive buying or selling lately and blamed the mark crosses and the weakness in dollar/yen for its decline, they said a dip below the 1.5000-mark level would be alarming.
"What you're getting is a lot of support on the bottom taken out gradually," the West Coast trader said.
Elsewhere, sterling volatilities were off early highs but stayed well bid as a resurgent spot cable climbed above $1.6500 earlier in Asian and European hours.
One-month cable implied volatility was a touch below late Thursday levels at 7.8/8.1 percent. The back end, which suffers less from time decay, was steady, with six-month quoted at 7.9/8.1 percent.
